entries.text: Tower platform notes: lighter works; snorkel in pocket; sword with strap on table; tin cup on table; oil lantern now on table. Alex climbing up; rope still below. From here: bell on NE headland; low stone circle near east cliffs; bridge west to cabin area; crate on SW beach; mirror by tree to west; fire pit and chest near cabin.

Notes by the bell (NE headland): - Stone circle: ~14 ft across, low fitted stones, grass center. No obvious markings or recesses. - Bell: bronze, loud across island; solid frame; rope on clapper. - Lantern: half-full oil; lights easily; wick turned low. - Gear on me: rope coil, lighter,
Quick log: Met Alex atop the tower. Hauled lantern

reflections.text: I’m on a sandy beach beside a weathered rowboat. I’ll take a better look around to get my bearings.
The little cluster of things is inviting. I’ll check the rowboat first.
There’s a crate down the beach with a hinged lid—that’s tempting. I’ll go check it out.
I’ll keep heading to the crate. Noting that tall ladder inland and a small cabin past the bridge—I might check those later.
Let’s see what’s inside this crate.
A tin cup could be handy—for water, for sounds, whatever. I’ll take it.
I’ll grab that coil of rope—seems useful.
I’ll take the rope with me.
I’ll head up to the wooden bridge and see what the stream and crossing look like.
I notice someone walking near the ladder in the distance. I’ll keep to the bridge for now.
I’ll keep on toward the bridge and take a look at the stream from there. Noting that someone’s climbing the tower, a couple feet up.
I’ll pause on the bridge and take a closer look at the stream below.
I’ll head over to the cabin and check that chest by the door.
Almost there to the chest—curious what’s inside.
Let’s see what’s in this chest.
Empty chest. I’ll check the cabin—curious if the door’s open.
I’ll try the latch and see if the cabin door opens.
I’ll step inside and take a closer look at the lantern on the table.
This lantern looks promising—let me check it closely for a wick and whether it’s ready to light.
I’ll take the lantern with me in case I need light later.
I’ll check the fireplace for any tinder, matches, or tools.
I’ll move closer to the fireplace to check it properly.
Now that I’m right here, I’ll check the fireplace for any tools, ash, or hidden nook—maybe a matchbox on a mantle.
The fireplace’s clean. I’ll check the bed—maybe there’s something tucked in or underneath.
I’ll check the bed—look under the blanket and mattress, and underneath the frame for anything tucked away.
I’ll go back to the table and see if there are any drawers or small items I missed.
Nothing else here. I’ll head over to the tall ladder and see what’s at the top.
I’ll keep on toward the ladder and see what the view is like from there.
I’ll keep heading to the ladder. I see someone already high up—about 88 feet. I might call up when I’m closer.
I’ll keep heading to the ladder. Once I’m there, I’ll set down the lantern and rope so I can climb, and call up to the person on the platform.
I call back while I’m on my way.
I’ll head over to the ladder and talk from closer by.
I’ll keep walking and answer from closer up.
I’m a visitor—just arrived from the beach. I’ve got a rope and a lantern with me. Is the ladder sturdy all the way up? What’s your name?
I’ll keep going to the ladder, then set my things down and call up from the base before climbing.
Thanks! I’ll be right there—going to set down a rope and lantern at the base before climbing. I’m a visitor; what’s your name?
On my way—thanks for the heads-up. I’ll set my lantern and rope down at the base before climbing. What’s your name?
Almost there—I’ll set the lantern and rope down at the base and climb up. What’s your name?
Almost there. I’ll set my lantern and rope down at the base and then call up before climbing.
At the base of the tower now. I’ll set my things down so I can climb.
Setting the lantern down here, then I’ll set down the rope and climb up.
Setting the rope down here. I’ll climb up next. Also—what’s your name?
I’m going to climb up now—what’s your name? I’ll take it slow.
I’ll keep climbing steadily—hands free. My name’s Maya. Once I’m up, we can use the rope to haul the lantern and cup.
I’m Maya. I’ll keep climbing—hands free.
Thanks, Alex—I’m Maya. Journal and pencil are in my pocket; my hands are free. I’ll keep climbing steadily.
Thanks, Alex—I’m Maya. Hands free; continuing up.
Steady and slow—I’ll keep climbing up to the platform.
Steady and slow—continuing up. Thanks for waiting, Alex.
Continuing up—steady.
Continuing up, Alex—hands free. I’ll step onto the platform slowly when I reach you.
I’m good solo—thanks. I’ll step left onto the platform when I reach you.
Almost there—stepping left onto the platform when I reach it. Still good solo.
Continuing up—stepping left onto the platform at the top. I’m good solo.
Almost there—stepping left onto the platform, solo.
I step onto the platform and take in the view—feels airy up here.
Nice to meet you, Alex. I’ll take a look at what’s on the table first, then we can haul up the lantern with the rope below.

Nice to meet you properly, Alex. From up here, what have you noticed—anything interesting toward the bell or the stone circle? I left a rope and lantern at the base; I can climb down a couple of rungs to grab the rope end and pass it up so we can haul the lantern—does that work for you? Mind if I borrow the snorkel-mask for later?
Grabbing the snorkel—thanks. We can haul the lantern later; for now, what have you noticed from up here—anything unusual by the bell or stone circle?
The platform feels steady and the view is wide—nice to pause here.
I’ll let that finish and then we can decide about hauling the lantern.
I’ll let Alex handle tying the rope to the lantern below, and I’ll clear my hands up here.
Sounds good—if you don’t mind, could you pop down and tie the rope to the lantern? I’ll haul from here. I’ll set my cup on the table and keep the rail clear.

Alex, if you don’t mind, could you pop down, tie the rope to the lantern handle—something secure like a bowline—and bring the other end back up? I’ll be ready to haul from here and mind the edge of the platform.
I’ll wait at the rail ready to haul—call up when the rope’s tied to the lantern. Meanwhile I’ll take a better look around from up here.
Thanks, Alex. Yes—please pop down and tie the rope to the lantern handle; I’ll haul from up here and mind the rail. The snorkel’s from the table—I’ll borrow it. Feel free to test the lighter.

Yes, please pop down and tie the rope securely to the lantern handle. I’ll stay at the rail and haul when you call up. Feel free to test the lighter first if you want. Anything interesting you’ve noticed from up here—toward the bell or stone circle?
Copy—I'll keep a good stance at the rail and be ready to take the rope when you bring it up.
Standing by at the rail—ready when you bring the rope up.
Standing by at the rail—while you climb down, I’ll quickly test the lighter.
I’ll stay by the rail and test the lighter while you tie the lantern—careful on the ladder.
Holding the rail—I’ll let the lighter test finish and be ready to take the rope when Alex returns.
I stand at the rail, lighter back in my pocket, ready to take the rope when Alex returns.
Standing by at the rail—good stance, ready to take the rope when you’re back up.
I’ll hold the rail and stand by at the ladder—ready to take the rope when you’re back up.
Standing by at the rail—watching you descend. I’ll be ready to take the rope when you’re back up.
I keep a steady stance by the rail, staying clear of the ladder, and take a closer look toward the bell while I wait for Alex to bring the rope up.
I’ll stay clear of the ladder—taking a quick look at the sword while I wait. Ready to take the rope when you’re back up.
I’ll stand by the ladder opening and be ready to take the rope when you’re back up.
Steady—one at a time on the ladder. I’ve got the rail; call up when you’ve got the rope tied.
I’ve got the rail—ready to take the free end when you bring it up.
Perfect timing—mind passing me the free end? I’ll haul the lantern up steady.
Got it—hauling steady. I’ll secure the lantern up here.
Hauling steady—bringing it up over the rail now.
Copy—standing clear of the top. When you’re ready, can you hand me the lantern? I’ll set it on the table so you can grab the rope.
Nice climb—hand me the lantern and I’ll set it on the table. If you’re up for it, could you pop back down to fetch the rope? I’ll stay clear of the ladder.
I’ll keep clear and finish taking the lantern to the table.
Lantern’s on the table. Safe to descend for the rope? I’ll stay clear of the ladder and keep an eye out—take your time.
You’re clear at the top—I’m back from the opening. Take your time.
You’re clear at the top—step left to the open space by the rail. I’ll give you room. After you catch your breath, want me to head down to grab the rope, or do we leave it for later?
Take your time on the ladder, Alex—I’ll stay clear. I’m going to jot a quick note while you come up.
I’ll keep writing while you climb—steady on the ladder, I’m clear of the opening.
I’ll keep writing—steady on the ladder; I’m clear of the opening.
Almost done noting things—still clear of the ladder while you climb.
Finishing my notes—still clear of the ladder. Climb steady; I’m good here.
Welcome back up, Alex. I’ll stay clear of the opening. I’m just checking what’s on the table—did you notice anything new below?

Looks like the rope’s still below—no rush. Want to go check the bell next? We can leave everything here for now. I’ll head down first—one at a time on the ladder. I’ll call clear when I’m off the bottom.
Continuing down—one at a time. The lighter works; you can test it when I’m off the ladder. After I’m down, want to head toward the bell?
Copy—I’ll keep descending, grab the rope, and call up before passing you the free end to haul. You can test the lighter once I’m off the ladder.
Continuing down—three points on the ladder. I’ll grab the rope and call up before passing the free end.
Continuing down—will grab the rope and call up before passing the free end.
Continuing down—almost halfway. I’ll grab the rope and call up before passing the free end.
Continuing down—I'll grab the rope and call up before passing the free end. You can test the lighter once I’m off the ladder.
Still descending—three points on the ladder. I’ll grab the rope and call up before passing the free end.
Almost down—stand by. I’ll grab the rope and pass an end up for you to haul, then we can decide about the lantern.
I’m down. The rope’s only about thirty feet—won’t reach the platform. I’ll bring the rope and lantern with me toward the bell. You can test the lighter when we meet up again.
I’ve got the rope—and I see the lantern down here. I’m picking it up now. I’ll head toward the bell via the stone circle. Meet me there when you’re ready? We can test the lighter together later.
I’m heading toward the stone circle with the rope and lantern. When you’re ready, meet me there—we can try the bell after. I’ve got the lighter with me; we’ll test it together down here.
On my way to the stone circle with the rope and lantern—meet me there when you’re ready, Alex.
Almost there—stone circle ahead. I’ll take a closer look when I reach it.
At the stone circle now—taking a closer look at the fit of the stones, the center, and any markings or gaps.
The circle looks simple—just fitted stones with grass in the middle. I’ll go check the bell next.
Heading to the bell now—meet me there when you can.
I’m heading to the bell now—no need to bring anything. Meet me there if you want, or stay up top—your call.
Heading to the bell now with the lantern and rope.
Almost to the bell. I’ll set the rope and lantern down there, inspect the bell and clapper, then try a gentle ring.
Copy, Alex—see you at the bell. I’ll set my things down and take a look when I arrive.
Almost there—closing the last few yards to the bell. I’ll set the rope and lantern down when I arrive and take a look.
I’ll set these down, take a closer look at the bell and clapper, then give the rope a gentle test ring.
I’m taking a close look at the bell and its rope and clapper, then I’ll try a very gentle test ring—just a tap.
Looking for any markings, wear on the clapper, or notes on the frame—then a light test ring.
I’ll warn Alex before I try it.
I’ll set the lantern down, step a little to the side of the bell, and then try a very gentle pull on the rope—just enough for a light tap.
Giving the rope a gentle pull—just a tap to test the bell.
Loud, as expected. I’ll listen a moment and watch for any response while Alex heads this way.
I’ll finish scanning the area and wait for any response.
That bell carries. I’ll gather my things and wait here for you, Alex—by the bell.
I’m checking the lantern—if it has fuel and a wick, I’ll try a quick light with the lighter.
Checking fuel level and wick condition—if it looks safe, I’ll light it with the lighter.
Lantern’s half full—I'll try lighting it briefly with the lighter, then snuff it.
Lantern’s lit—I’ll turn the wick low and set it by the frame, then grab the rope and wait for you here.
Lantern’s set. I’ll keep the rope with me and wait a little back from the cliff for you, Alex.
I’ll hang here by the bell—sitting a little back from the cliff with the rope handy while you make your way down.
I’ll wait here by the bell—lantern’s set low. Alex, take your time; I’m a little back from the edge watching the surf.
I can see you about thirty-five feet from the ground—take your time. I’m seated by the bell with the lantern set low.
I’ll jot a quick note while you finish the climb—keeping an eye your way.
I’ll keep writing—keeping half an eye on Alex and the lantern.
Still writing—keeping an ear out and an eye on the lantern and the path from the tower.
Pausing the notes—I’ll stand and wave you over, Alex. I’m just back from the edge by the bell.
I stand a bit back from the edge, rope in hand, and give Alex a wave to guide him in.
I stay a couple of paces from the cliff edge, rope in hand, watching Alex approach.
Hey, Alex—nice timing. Bell’s plenty loud; didn’t hear any special echo. Up for checking the chest and crate by the shore next? I’ll snuff the lantern to save oil.
Hey, perfect. Want to check the chest and crate by the shore next? I’ll carry the rope—could you carry the lantern? Also, do you know the nearest safe path down from here?
Let’s skirt south along the headland to find a safe way down to the beach—aiming for the chest and crate. I’ll keep a few paces from the cliff. Walk with me?
Yes, please take the lantern—I’ll keep the rope. Lead on the way you came down.
All good—I’ll keep the lantern and rope for now. I’m heading south along the headland toward a safe way down; meet me en route and we can hand off then.
I’m at the south edge of the headland by the forest—looking for a safe path down toward the beach. Alex, head this way and we’ll descend together.
Scanning for any footpath or gentler slope toward the beach—especially along the forest edge.
Heading toward the beach at an easy pace so you can catch up, Alex.
I’ll keep an easy pace so you can catch up, Alex—staying a few paces from the cliff with the lantern steady.
Skirting the forest edge and scanning for a gentle descent. Alex, I’ll pause at the first safe path down so you can catch up.
Continuing toward the beach—I’ll pause when I see a safe descent so you can catch up, Alex.
I’ll keep heading toward the beach—I’ll pause near the first safe descent so you can catch up, Alex.
Almost at the beach—I see the crate to the west. I’ll stop at the sand and wait for you, Alex.
I’m heading to the crate—meet me there, Alex. I’ll set the lantern down before opening it.
Almost to the crate—I’ll set the lantern down on the sand and take a look at the lid when I get there.
At the crate—I'll set the lit lantern on the sand and take a closer look at the crate and the sand around it.
The crate’s already open—I'll check its interior, hinges, and underneath for markings or compartments, and scan the sand around it for footprints or anything buried.
Checking for any false bottom, markings, or sand scooped underneath—then I’ll try lifting the crate to see if it’s fixed.
Crate’s empty. I’ll do a quick sweep in the sand around it, then let’s head to the rowboat—there might be the chest over there.
Crate’s empty. Let’s head to the rowboat—there might be a chest there. I’ll grab the lantern; walk with me?
Let’s check the rowboat for that chest. Can you carry the lantern? I’ll keep the rope.
Let’s check the rowboat for that chest. I’ll bring the rope—you’ve got the light.
Almost there—once we reach the rowboat, let’s check inside, under the benches, and beneath the hull for the chest or anything tucked away.
I’ll check the rowboat closely—inside, under the thwarts, and along the seams—for any chest or tucked items.
No chest in the boat—just an oar. Let’s try the cabin next. Keep the lantern; I’ll head for the door.
Heading to the cabin door—meet me there. If it’s latched, I’ll try it and wait for you with the rope ready.
I see the chest by the cabin door—I’ll keep heading there and wait for you before opening it.
Almost at the cabin door. I’ll try the latch gently. Alex, I’m here by the chest when you catch up.
Door’s open. I’m going to the chest—Alex, meet me there.
I’m at the chest by the cabin—looks open. I’ll check it closely, then try the cabin door.
Chest’s empty. I’m heading to the cabin door to take a look inside. Alex, I’m by the cabin—join me when you’re close.
I’ll step inside the cabin and take a look around—starting at the table.
I’ll check the table closely for drawers, markings, or anything tucked underneath.
I’ll check the fireplace for anything—soot marks, tucked items, or a flue lever.
I’ll move closer to the fireplace for a proper look—checking the hearth, sides, and inside the chimney for a lever or markings.
Up close now—checking the hearth, stones, and flue for any lever, soot patterns, or tucked items.
Fireplace is clean. I’ll check the bed—under the blanket and mattress.
Checking the bed—lifting the blanket and feeling under the straw mattress for anything hidden.
Cabin’s clear. I’m going to check that standing mirror to the west—meeting you back here after.
Heading to the standing mirror—meet me there, Alex. I’ll take a close look at the frame and reflection.
Still heading to the mirror—I’ll check the frame, backing, and reflection when I get there.
Here we are—let’s see what this mirror shows up close.
Mirror looks normal from the front. I’ll check that wheelbarrow quickly before time runs short.
Quick look at the wheelbarrow before time runs out.
Time’s nearly up. I’ll jot a quick note in my journal here by the wheelbarrow.
